_note: The registry of paper page layouts. Read by layout.py (emits iflayout.def for the class) and by the production pipeline's article converter (table, figure and sidebar behavior). Add a layout here and document it in docs/paper-layouts.md; no other file changes. Numbers are inches and points. Spec 0017 FR-030.

two-column.summary: The house default. Two 3.36 in columns, 9.5/12.4 pt, 0.75 in margins. Wide figures and tables span both columns.
two-column.modeled_on: Between Nature and NEJM; a little more open than either.
two-column.best_for: Papers light on figures and tables, or whose figures and tables fit inside a column.

two-column-dense.summary: The densest two-column page. Two 3.55 in columns with a 0.17 in gutter, 8.6/11.2 pt, 0.6 in margins.
two-column-dense.modeled_on: Nature: 89 mm columns, 8.2/10.8 pt, margins about 0.55 in.
two-column-dense.best_for: Long papers that must stay short in pages; text-led work with compact figures.

two-column-wide-margin.summary: Two 3.15 in columns at 10/12.4 pt with a wide inside margin (1.2 in) and a 0.85 in outside margin. The most open two-column page.
two-column-wide-margin.modeled_on: NEJM: 10/12 pt on narrow columns with a wide inner margin.
two-column-wide-margin.best_for: Short, text-led papers; a reader who will annotate or bind the page.

single-sidebar.summary: A 4.85 in main column (about 77 characters at 9.5 pt) with a 2.0 in sidebar. Pull quotes, practical tests, and notes sit in the sidebar. Wide figures and tables span the full 7.1 in.
single-sidebar.modeled_on: JAMA Network Open: a wide main column beside a narrow side column.
single-sidebar.best_for: Papers heavy in tables and figures, and papers with many callouts.

single-sidebar-compact.summary: A 5.2 in main column (about 83 characters at 9.5 pt) with a 1.6 in sidebar. Wide figures and tables span 7.05 in.
single-sidebar-compact.modeled_on: JAMA Network Open, with a narrower side column.
single-sidebar-compact.best_for: Callout-heavy papers that need a longer line and a slimmer sidebar.

single-narrow-margin.summary: One column across the page, 7.0 in wide, 9/12.6 pt, 0.75 in margins. The densest single-column page. Callouts stay inline.
single-narrow-margin.modeled_on: None of the four reference publications sets one wide column across the page; this layout follows no reference.
single-narrow-margin.best_for: Table- and figure-heavy work with short paragraphs, where a wide page serves the exhibits. Not for long prose.
single-narrow-margin.caution: About 105 characters per line at 9 pt, above the 90 characters a reader follows comfortably. Use it only when the content is mostly exhibits and short paragraphs.

two-column-sidebar.summary: Two 2.65 in text columns with a 0.17 in gutter beside a 1.6 in sidebar band, 9/11.6 pt, 0.6 in outer margins. The sidebar holds short notes, pull quotes, and callouts; wide figures and tables span the band and both columns.
two-column-sidebar.modeled_on: The Lancet (about 1.1 in outer band, alternating sides), BMJ (about 1.5 in left band, every page), and HBR (1.75 in sidebar column). Measured 2026-10-01.
two-column-sidebar.best_for: Dense papers with many short callouts that must stay two-column.
two-column-sidebar.note: Planned. LaTeX places margin material beside a two-column text block unreliably; this layout needs a different technique and is not built. Selecting it fails the build and names the alternatives.

two-column-science.summary: Two 3.57 in columns with a 0.17 in gutter, 8.2/10.6 pt, 0.6 in margins.
two-column-science.modeled_on: Science (Reports): 3.53 in columns, 8/10.5 pt, 0.51 in margins.
two-column-science.best_for: Short, compact papers with small figures.

two-column-pnas.summary: Two 3.4 in columns with a 0.18 in gutter, 9/11 pt, 0.76 in margins.
two-column-pnas.modeled_on: PNAS: 3.40 in columns, 9/10 pt (leading opened to 11 pt here), 0.54 to 0.60 in margins.
two-column-pnas.best_for: General research papers; a balanced, moderately dense page.

two-column-cell.summary: Two 3.32 in columns with a 0.17 in gutter, 8.5/10.9 pt, 0.8 in margins.
two-column-cell.modeled_on: Cell: 3.32 in columns, 8.5/10.9 pt, margins 0.74 to 0.83 in.
two-column-cell.best_for: Research papers with many figure panels; a dense page with firm margins.

two-column-large.summary: Two 3.3 in columns with a 0.22 in gutter, 10/12 pt, 0.85 in margins. The largest two-column type.
two-column-large.modeled_on: AHA's Circulation: 10/12 pt on 3.26 in columns, 0.68 in margins (NAR: 10/11 pt on 3.43 in).
two-column-large.best_for: Papers read on screen or by readers who want larger type.

single-sidebar-left.summary: A 5.64 in main column (about 83 characters at 9/12.2 pt) with a 1.84 in sidebar on the left. Callouts sit in the left sidebar; wide figures and tables span the full 7.5 in.
single-sidebar-left.modeled_on: eLife: 5.64 in column, 9/12.2 pt, a 1.84 in left sidebar. Scientific Reports is similar (5.5 in column, 1.6 in left band, 9/10 pt).
single-sidebar-left.best_for: Long-form papers where the reader scans the sidebar first; callout-heavy papers.

single-sidebar-left-wide.summary: A 5.22 in main column (about 76 characters at 10/13.2 pt) with a 2.0 in sidebar on the left. Wide figures and tables span 7.5 in.
single-sidebar-left-wide.modeled_on: PLOS ONE: 5.22 in column, 10/13 pt, a 2.28 in left sidebar.
single-sidebar-left-wide.best_for: Long-form papers with generous callouts; the most open sidebar page.

three-column.summary: Three 2.28 in text columns, 8.7/10.5 pt, 0.51 in margins. The densest page set.
three-column.modeled_on: Science Research Articles (measured: 3 columns of 2.28 in with a 0.2 in gutter).
three-column.best_for: Long, text-dense papers where page count matters most.
three-column.note: Planned. LaTeX has no native three-column mode that handles floats; this needs multicol and a custom float solution. Selecting it fails the build.
